note: The analysis a briefing agent would write after reading the six sample articles. Fictional.

items.title: CI secret stealer pushed through hijacked accounts
items.reason: active campaign; erases its own traces
items.what_happened: Attackers using stolen GitHub accounts push a branch and commit that add a secret-dumping workflow. The workflow deletes its own run afterwards.
items.quote: This campaign is active and spreading.
items.who: anyone with write access to GitHub repos that run Actions
steps: Search every repo for branches matching `ci-helper-NNNN` and commits titled `chore: add ci helper` (the run does this for you).
If found: rotate every secret those workflows could read, then review recent workflow runs for gaps in run numbers.
items.action: Check repos for `ci-helper-NNNN` branches; rotate CI secrets if found

items.title: Fake job interviews deliver malware through look-alike npm packages
items.reason: malware in packages developers install directly
items.what_happened: A fake hiring company told developers to install look-alike UI animation packages that steal credentials on install. Some also add a VS Code task that runs when a folder opens.
items.quote: Treat any machine that installed them as compromised.
items.who: developers who run take-home tests or install UI animation plugins
steps: Search lockfiles for the exact names `occupai-demo-anim` and `occupai-demo-anim-js` (not substrings: `occupai-demo-animate` is legitimate).
Look for `.vscode/tasks.json` with `"runOn": "folderOpen"`; turn off VS Code `task.allowAutomaticTasks`.
If found: remove the package and rotate every credential on that machine.

items.title: Node.js security releases; Node 20 is end-of-life
items.reason: remotely triggerable server bugs; fixes available
items.what_happened: Node.js 22.23.5 and 24.22.3 fix several high-severity HTTP/2 and TLS issues. Node 20 gets no fixes.
items.quote: Node.js 20 is end-of-life and receives no fixes.
items.who: anyone running Node servers, CI or local tooling
steps: Run `node -v` and update to 22.23.5 / 24.22.3 or newer.
Move exact pins (`.nvmrc`, workflow `node-version`, Dockerfile `FROM node:`) to a fixed version, or a major only in CI.
items.action: Update Node to 22.23.5 / 24.22.3; fix exact pins (`node -v`)
items.why: HTTP/2 and TLS fixes; 20 is EOL

items.title: Next.js security release (cache leak)
items.what_happened: Next.js 16.4.5 and 15.5.29 fix a cache leak that can serve one user's page to another. No exploitation reported.
items.quote: There is no evidence of exploitation.
steps: In each Next.js project: `npm install next@16.4.5` (or `next@15.5.29` on 15.x) in a branch, build and test, then redeploy.
items.why: one user's page served to another

items.title: Apache httpd HTTP/2 module flaw
items.reason: serious but not exploited; only matters if you run httpd
items.what_happened: A race condition in an HTTP/2 module can corrupt memory in httpd 2.4.55 to 2.4.70. Version 2.4.71 fixes it.
items.who: anyone self-hosting Apache httpd with HTTP/2
steps: Only if you run httpd: upgrade to 2.4.71, or set `Protocols http/1.1` as a stopgap.
items.action: Only if you run httpd: upgrade to 2.4.71

items.title: Hosting provider env-var breach
items.reason: contained breach; AI keys in env vars are a target
items.what_happened: A hosting provider says attackers decrypted environment variables for some workspaces and ran up fraudulent AI usage.
items.quote: Customers should rotate stored secrets and set spend limits on AI keys.
items.who: customers of that provider; anyone storing AI keys as env vars
steps: If you use that provider: rotate stored secrets.
Everyone: set spend limits and usage alerts on AI provider keys.
items.action: Set spend limits on AI provider keys; rotate if you used the provider
items.why: stolen AI keys get abused fast
